307, 504 R/W SEC.149 OF IPC ON THE FILE OF THE PRINCIPAL SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND CJM MYSURU.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR ORDERS,
THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER Petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 6 have preferred this petition under Section 438 of Cr.P.C., praying to enlarge them on anticipatory bail in Crime No.22/2023 of Mysuru South Police Station, registered for offences punishable under Sections 143, 147, 148, 341, 324, 307, 504 read with 149 of IPC.
2.
Heard the learned counsel for petitioners and learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent- State and perused the material on record.

In the complaint lodged by one Doddegowda M.D. S/o Doddegowda, he has alleged that on 27.01.2023 at about 9.45 pm, while he was returning to his house from his office, all the accused wrongfully restrained him and with an intention to commit his murder assaulted him with knife,
iron rod and clubs and caused bleeding injuries to him.
4. The learned counsel for petitioners has contended that the complainant is none other than the son-in-law of accused No.4.

The relationship between the complainant and his wife, one Smt.Jyothi is not cordial and in this connection, she has lodged a complaint against him on 22.09.2022, which is registered in Crime No.38/2022 of Mysuru Women Police Station, for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506 read with 34 of IPC.

He contends that even the complainant has lodged the complaint against his wife and her family members, which is registered in Crime No.143/2022 of Jayapura Police Station, for the offence punishable under Sections 143, NC:
2023:KHC:20435 147, 504, 323, 324, 355, 327 read with 149 of IPC.

Hence, he contends that in view Basappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 14 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82161202/
2 of the said ill-will, now false case is foisted against Accused No.4 and his family members.

sentences.text: He submits that petitioners are ready and willing to co-operate with the investigation and abide by any conditions and therefore, seeks to allow the petition.

5. The learned High Court Government Pleader contends that investigation is in progress and in the event of grant of anticipatory bail to the petitioners, they may not co-operate with the investigation.
He further contends that complainant has sustained injuries, which shows he has been assaulted by the petitioners.
Therefore, he seeks to reject the petition.
6. Incident is alleged to have taken place on 27.01.2023 at about 9.45 pm.
The complaint is lodged on the next day at about 8.00 pm.
It is stated by the complainant that, he became unconscious, and then he was admitted at K.R.Hospital, Mysuru.

Perusal of the NC: 2023:KHC:20435 wound certificate shows that he has sustained the following injuries:
1) Linear laceration over upper 3rd of left arm 2) abrasion over stomach 3) abrasion over forehead
The above injuries are stated to be simple in nature.
It is alleged that all the accused with an intention to commit his murder, assaulted him with deadly weapons like knife, iron rod and clubs.
Looking at the nature of injuries sustained, prima facie it doesn't appear to have been caused with deadly weapons, as alleged.
However, it is a matter to be investigated and established in due course.
Considering the prior complaints and cases registered against each other and considering the nature of injuries, relief sought by the petitioners can be granted by imposing necessary conditions.
Hence, the following ORDER Petition is allowed.

NC: 2023:KHC:20435 Petitioners/accused Nos.1 to 6 in Crime No.22/2023 of Mysuru South Police Station, shall be released in the event of their arrest subject to following conditions:
a) They shall appear before the Investigation Officer within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a copy of the order and shall execute a bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) each with two sureties for the likesum.
b) They shall furnish proof of their residential address and shall inform the Investigation Officer/Court, if there is any change in the address.
c) They shall be available for the purpose of investigation as and when required and shall co-operate with the investigation.
d) They shall not leave the jurisdiction of the trial Court without prior permission till completion of the investigation of the case.

e) They shall not tamper with the  prosecution witnesses either directly or Basappa vs The State Of Karnataka on 14 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82161202/
3  indirectly.
